prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band; (b) this is a ZOOMED-IN close-up composition — the tapeworm character, the dog and the suitcase must run past the edges of the square, filling the whole frame; (c) NO decorative starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays or sunbeam rays anywhere.

SCENE: A big, friendly, cheerful cartoon TAPEWORM character fills the picture on a diagonal: its body is a long FLAT ribbon made of large rectangular segments joined end to end like the carriages of a little train, gently curving across the frame and running off the bottom and the right edge of the picture. Its round, smiling head (two dot eyes, rosy cheek circles, a happy smile) wears a tiny zig-zag party crown on top — and on each side of the head sit two big round suction cups, drawn as simple thick circles, like little stuck-on bath-toy suckers, four circles in total. The tapeworm carries a tiny old-fashioned SUITCASE in a curled tip of its ribbon body and waves goodbye with a small kerchief — it is cheerfully leaving on a trip. Next to it, a happy, good-natured cartoon DOG (floppy ears, wagging tail drawn mid-wag, tongue out in a smile) sits proudly, one front paw raised in a friendly goodbye wave, partly running off the left edge. From the top corner a single friendly, simple, short-sleeved cartoon HAND (just the hand and a bit of sleeve, no full human body or face) reaches in holding a BIG ROUND chunky TABLET character — a speckled disc with its own small cheerful face (two dot eyes, a little smile). Everything large, simple, chunky and warm, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in — the big rectangular tapeworm segments are perfect colouring fields.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere. They leave a big empty shape that cannot be removed afterwards.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, or vignette (other than the suitcase's own small case shape and the tapeworm's own segments, which are characters and body parts, not a frame around the whole picture). The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge — the tapeworm, dog, hand and suitcase are CUT OFF by the image edge itself where they extend past it.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — parts of the tapeworm's ribbon body, the dog, the hand/sleeve or the suitcase run right off the top, bottom, left and right edges, with no white margin band and no enclosing outline.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO teeth, no fangs, no scary hooks, no syringe, no blood, no sick or sad animal, nothing gruesome — the tiny party crown is a cheerful crown shape, not spikes.
- NO full human figure, no human face or body — only a single friendly hand and sleeve reaching in from off-frame.
- Do NOT draw the tapeworm inside the dog or near the dog's tummy — it is simply leaving the scene like a departing guest, waving cheerfully, clearly harmless in this picture.
